patch_description: The current program regressed from 2.25 to 2.13. The regression came from the new "corner" moves: pushing two-wall-touching circles diagonally into corners is wrong for this hex layout — most wall-touching circles here touch exactly one wall, and the tol-based classification misfires, systematically dragging circles out of the LP-optimal lattice. Two fixes: (1) revert the directed move to the proven "push away from the wall you touch" rule (this was the 0.86-scoring version), and (2) add a cheap final greedy sweep after the hill-climb: for each circle, try small ±deltas in x and y, re-solve the LP, and keep any improvement. This directly exploits the fact that the LP gives exact optimal radii for given centers, so any center move that helps is measurable; the greedy pass polishes irregular placements the random hill-climb misses (the headroom identified in the analysis). Also raise iteration count slightly since each LP solve is fast (~ms).
